build.rationale: Compiles packages and produces executable/object files to disk.

clean.rationale: Removes build artifacts and caches, but effects are reversible by rebuilding/re-downloading.

env.rationale: Reads environment by default but can modify persistent settings with -w/-u flags.

generate.rationale: Creates or updates Go source files via directives in existing files.

get.rationale: Modifies go.mod to add/upgrade/remove dependencies and downloads modules.

install.rationale: Compiles packages and installs executables to filesystem (typically $GOBIN).

list.rationale: Lists packages or modules without modifying state.

mod.rationale: Module maintenance command group; subcommands can modify go.mod, create vendor dirs, and edit module metadata.

mod download.rationale: Downloads modules into the local module cache, which modifies local state but is bounded and reversible.

mod edit.rationale: Modifies the go.mod file by applying editing operations, which is reversible.

mod graph.rationale: Prints the module requirement graph without modifying any files.

mod init.rationale: Creates a new go.mod file in the current directory, which is reversible.

mod tidy.rationale: Modifies go.mod and go.sum to match source code dependencies, which is reversible.

mod vendor.rationale: Creates or resets the vendor directory with needed packages, which is reversible.

mod verify.rationale: Verifies that downloaded modules have not been modified, without making any changes.

mod why.rationale: Shows import graph paths to packages, without modifying any state.

run.rationale: Compiles and executes code, creating temporary compilation artifacts.

run package.rationale: Compiles and runs a Go program, which may have side effects but is typical development behavior.

version.rationale: Prints version information without modifying state.
